bihar_raw_news.title: FM Sitharaman pitches for India as manufacturing, innovation hub
bihar_raw_news.content: International 31 Aug, 2026 FM Sitharaman pitches for India as manufacturing, innovation hub Business To Business, New Delhi, 31 August 2026: Union Minister of Finance and Corporate Affairs Nirmala Sitharaman on Monday called on 3M to deepen its investments in research and development, advanced manufacturing and local supply-chain development in India as she pitched the country as an increasingly important hub for technology, innovation and global manufacturing. Taking to the social media platform X, the Ministry of Finance said the minister made the remarks during a meeting with 3M Chairman and CEO William Brown on the sidelines of the G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors (FMCBG) meeting in Asheville, North Carolina, today. The discussions focused on ways to deepen the US multinational's engagement with India as the country evolves beyond being a large consumer market into a platform for advanced manufacturing, technology and innovation, the ministry said in a post on X. The two sides also discussed data security and ways to optimise the engagement of India's talent pool within domestic enterprise ecosystems. In addition, Brown appreciated the availability of a deep talent pool in India and said there were significant opportunities for technology development as well as local markets. He also acknowledged the support extended by the Indian government as part of its broader economic and structural reforms, according to the ministry. The Finance Minister said there was considerable scope for 3M to expand localisation, R&D, and technology development in India by leveraging the country's talent and manufacturing capabilities. She said regional innovation could help 3M serve not only the domestic market but also wider global and Asia-Pacific supply chains. The Finance Minister also called for greater investment by the company in R&D, advanced manufacturing capabilities and the development of local supply-chain networks. FM Sitharaman acknowledged 3M's continued confidence in the Indian economy and suggested avenues for further expansion of its presence in the country. The meeting was held as FM Sitharaman participates in the G20 FMCBG meeting and associated engagements in Asheville over the next two days. Moreover, the Finance Minister arrived at Greenville-Spartanburg International Airport in South Carolina earlier and was received by India's Ambassador to the US Vinay Mohan Kwatra. bihar_raw_news.title: 40 nursing colleges in Bihar lose Indian Nursing Council recognition over infrastructure ...
bihar_raw_news.content: 40 nursing colleges in Bihar lose Indian Nursing Council recognition over infrastructure, faculty deficiencies Written By : Adity Saha Published On 2026-09-01T13:15:22+05:30 | Updated On 1 Sept 2026 1:15 PM IST Nalanda: Altogether 40 nursing colleges lost their recognition from the Indian Nursing Council (INC) due to deficiencies, including inadequate infrastructure and unqualified teaching staff found during inspections. The affected institutions include both government and private nursing colleges offering courses such as ANM, GNM and BSc Nursing. The council took the action under Section 14 of the Indian Nursing Council Act, 1947. Among the affected institutions are three prominent nursing institutes in Nalanda district. The Bhagwan Mahavir Institute of Medical Sciences (BMIMS), Pawapuri, which lost its recognition for BSc Nursing course; the Gautam Institute of Nursing at Saiyad Bahri on Chandi-Hilsa Road lost recognition for both its ANM and GNM courses; and the GNM School of Nursing at Sadar Hospital, Chhoti Pahari, Bihar Sharif, is also on the list. The action has also affected nursing institutions attached to major government medical colleges. These include the GNM nursing institution at Patna Medical College and Hospital (PMCH) and the School of Nursing (GNM) at Bhagalpur Medical College Hospital. Also read- Nursing Institute Inspections must be done by Councils only: Karnataka HC During inspection of these institutions, the council found that several private colleges were operating from just two rooms and some teaching staff did not have the required degrees. Speaking to ETV Bharat , Bihar Nursing Registration Council president Dr Rekha Jha said the institutions can regain recognition after addressing the deficiencies pointed out during the inspection. Once the required standards are met, the colleges can apply for a fresh inspection, following which the INC may restore their recognition. However, the withdrawal of recognition has put the future of thousands of nursing students in Bihar in uncertainty. Dr Jha said students studying at institutions whose recognition has been cancelled will not be eligible for recruitment in major Central government hospitals, AIIMS and the Railways. She added that the withdrawal of recognition would also affect students seeking higher education or professional practice abroad. They would also be unable to register with nursing councils in other states and would be excluded from nursing vacancies outside Bihar. "Such action was taken because institutions were found to be ignoring prescribed standards. The department has taken this action retrospectively. As a result, students obtaining degrees from these institutions will not be eligible for government jobs," Dr Jha said. bihar_raw_news.content: Home Videos Society Nepal Floods | How Gandak Barrage Protected Bihar From Floods Nepal Floods | How Gandak Barrage Protected Bihar From Floods By Video Team - The Better India 01 Sep 2026 By Video Team - The Better India 01 Sep 2026 Follow Us New Update A massive flood surge from Nepal reached Bihar. 🌊 After catastrophic flooding in Nepal sent a huge surge through the Trishuli and Narayani rivers, the water flowed into the Gandak River and reached Bihar. At Valmikinagar, engineers opened all 36 gates of the 60-year-old Gandak Barrage, releasing nearly 1.5 lakh cusecs of water in a controlled manner to manage the sudden surge. Advertisment The barrage became a crucial part of the effort to manage the rising Gandak River floodwaters. But downstream villages still faced flooding and evacuations, highlighting just how powerful and unpredictable extreme flood events can be. It also raises an important question: can infrastructure built 60 years ago still play a critical role in protecting communities today? bihar_raw_news.title: Plans afoot to take bullet train project to UP and Bihar , will make it possible to travel between ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Plans afoot to take bullet train project to UP and Bihar, will make it possible to travel between Delhi and Patna in 4.5 hours: Railways Minister ANI 01 Sep 2026, 00:35 GMT+10 New Delhi [India], August 31 (ANI): Travel between Delhi and Lucknow will be reduced to two hours and that between the national capital and Patna to 4.5 hours in the proposed bullet train project covering major cities in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, Railway Minister Ashwani Vaishnaw said on Monday. Speaking during the inauguration of newly converted and electrified broad-gauge rail line on the Nepalganj Road-Nanpara-Bahraich section, Vaishnaw said that the proposed bullet train corridor will include Agra, Kanpur, Lucknow, Varanasi and Patna and connect these sprawling cities to Delhi. He said the proposed project will drastically cut travel time between the national capital and major cities of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. The minister said under the project, the estimated travel time between Delhi and Agra (200 km) will be 58 minutes . Time to reach Kanpur from Delhi (455 km) will be 1 hour 50 minutes; the route to Lucknow (495 km) will be 2 hours 12 minutes and it will take three hours to reach Prayagraj (750 km) from the national capital. The proposed bullet train will take about 3 hours 33 minutes to reach Varanasi from Delhi (945 km) and 4.5 hours (1,170 km) to reach Patna. 'If the project materialises, it will be the next phase bullet train corridor in the country after the Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor and the first to connect the National Capital with many cities of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar,' Vaisnaw said. The proposed corridor will not only provide a huge relief to lakhs of daily passengers but is also expected to boost tourism, business and economic activity across the Delhi-UP-Bihar belt, especially in religious tourism hubs like Agra, Prayagraj, Varanasi, Gorakhpur and Patna. Currently, the highest design speed in the Indian railway network is around 180 kmph, achieved by semi-high-speed services such as Vande Bharat. Against this, the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail (MAHSR) Project has a design speed of 350 kmph and an operational speed of 320 kmph. It is one of the most extensive rail infrastructure programmes undertaken in India, and will connect Mumbai and Ahmedabad in about 1 hour 58 minutes. The first high-speed rail service in the country is expected to commence in August 2027 and the first section to be opened will be from Surat to Vapi. Speaking after the launch of Semicon 2.0, the minister said the initiative will focus not only on semiconductor manufacturing but also on developing talent, chip design, equipment, materials, advanced packaging and research and development. national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will address the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan, today. The Summit is being held to mark the 25th anniversary of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation. The SCO has ten member countries, including China and Russia. India has been a full member of the SCO since 2017. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his address to the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit, will underline India’s priorities in the areas of security, connectivity and opportunity. India has consistently opposed double standards in the fight against terrorism, separatism and extremism. India believes that greater connectivity among member countries is essential for peace and prosperity in the region. At the same time, connectivity projects must respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries. India has also been emphasising the need to create new opportunities for the youth of member countries and promote the startup ecosystem. India believes that the energy, innovation and entrepreneurship of young people can give a fresh impetus to regional development and cooperation. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, on the first day of his two-day visit to Kyrgyzstan yesterday, held bilateral meetings with the leaders of Russia, Iran, the Kyrgyz Republic and Armenia on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit in Bishkek. The meetings covered various aspects of bilateral relations and issues of mutual interest. The Prime Minister also attended the official opening ceremony of the sixth World Nomad Games in Bishkek yesterday evening, along with leaders of other SCO member countries. The biennial sporting event celebrates the rich sporting traditions, culture and heritage of nomadic civilisations.

national_raw_news.title: 45 mins ago | International 46 New Delhi rejects Court of Arbitration award on Indus Water Treaty
national_raw_news.content: India has strongly rejected a ruling by the World Bank-constituted Court of Arbitration over the Indus Waters Treaty, rejecting the tribunal’s authority and calling its decisions legally invalid. In a social media post, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said India has never recognised the arbitration panel, did not participate in its proceedings and would not be bound by its rulings. New Delhi also reiterated that the Indus Waters Treaty remains in abeyance. The statement came after the Court of Arbitration in The Hague ruled that India’s reasons for putting the treaty on hold did not justify its suspension or termination. The panel called on India to continue observing its obligations under the 1960 water-sharing agreement. India, however, rejected the ruling, arguing that the arbitration panel itself was established in violation of the terms of the treaty. The MEA said the panel has no jurisdiction whatsoever over India’s sovereign decisions concerning the treaty or its infrastructure projects. New Delhi suspended the Indus Waters Treaty following the Pahalgam terror attack in April last year, citing national security concerns and continued cross-border terrorism. India has maintained that its decision on the treaty is a sovereign matter and that statements or rulings by the arbitration panel will not affect its actions related to water and infrastructure projects.

national_raw_news.title: 54 mins ago | International 28 Nepal rescuers blast hillside in search of hydropower workers
national_raw_news.content: Rescue teams in Nepal are racing against time to reach more than 600 workers believed to be trapped in mud-filled tunnels at the Trishuli-3A hydropower site. Crews are using explosives, heavy machinery and air pumps to clear the tunnels and search for survivors. According to Nepal’s disaster management authority, 939 people have died, and 3,925 are missing, including 592 foreign nationals. So far, 279 people have been rescued from hydropower sites, while more than 11,000 people have been rescued across the country. The rescue operation is being supported by Nepalese and Chinese military teams, along with experts from India, South Korea and Australia. Severe flooding and landslides have made it difficult for rescuers to locate the buried tunnels. India has sent specialised teams to help with both rescue operations and the identification of victims. A 19-member Indian forensic team began work in Kathmandu, assisting with DNA testing to identify recovered remains. An Indian tunnel-rescue team is also working at hydropower sites in Chilime and Langtang. Experts are helping Nepalese authorities search for 933 workers and employees who have been missing since August 26, with many believed to be trapped inside the tunnels. At least 11 hydropower projects were damaged by the floods. Families say rescue efforts have been too slow and are urging authorities to act quickly. Downstream in Chitwan, nearly 300 bodies have been recovered from rivers. Many remain unidentified, so authorities are using DNA testing. Due to a shortage of freezers, some bodies have been temporarily buried until they can be identified. Nepal has asked several countries for help, including freezers, DNA-testing equipment, drones, bridges and specialised tunnel-rescue tools. A team of 18 Indian forensic experts is assisting with DNA identification. In Tibet, Chinese state media reports 16 deaths and 546 missing people. China has rejected claims that its hydropower projects caused the disaster, calling such allegations malicious speculation. The floods, believed to have been triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border, have caused widespread destruction, damaging homes, roads, bridges and hydropower infrastructure across Nepal.
